narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed, and the assessment found a 56% likelihood that you represent a credit risk — a figure that, while not overwhelmingly high, was sufficient to result in a denial. This means the decision was not clear-cut, and your profile contains both concerning and reassuring elements that pulled the outcome in different directions.

The single most influential factor working against your application was the size of the loan you requested. At 10,623 DM, your requested amount is dramatically higher than the average of roughly 2,887 DM seen among applicants who were approved — more than three times as much. Given that average yearly salaries in Germany at this time ranged from 10,000 to 20,000 DM, this is a substantial sum, and the model identified it as the strongest signal pointing toward risk. A larger loan simply means a larger obligation, and when combined with other factors in your profile, it raised serious concerns about repayability.

The second most important factor was the status of your checking account, which currently shows a negative balance. While it is true that nearly 20% of approved applicants also had a negative checking account balance, this feature still pushed your assessment toward the higher-risk category. A negative balance suggests that your current financial situation may already be under strain, making it harder to take on additional debt responsibly.

Interestingly, your credit history — which is classified as "critical or other credits" — actually worked in your favor, nudging the prediction slightly toward a better outcome. This category is quite common among approved applicants, with about 35% of them sharing a similar credit history, so this aspect of your profile is not unusual and did provide some counterbalance to the negative signals.

Beyond these top three factors, several other elements of your profile are worth noting. Your requested loan duration of 30 months is notably longer than the 19-month average for approved applicants, and you currently hold three existing credits at this bank compared to an average of about one and a half among those who were approved. You also have two financially dependent people, compared to an average of just over one among approved applicants, which adds further pressure to your financial obligations. Living in housing provided for free and having no property assets also placed you in a less common position compared to most approved applicants.

On the positive side, your long employment history of seven or more years is a genuine strength, and your job in management or a highly skilled field speaks well of your earning stability. These are meaningful positives that likely prevented the predicted risk from being even higher.

To improve your chances in a future application, you might consider requesting a smaller loan amount, as this was the most decisive factor in the denial. Bringing your checking account into a positive balance before reapplying would also significantly strengthen your profile. Additionally, reducing the number of existing credits or shortening the requested loan duration could help present a more manageable financial picture to the assessment process.
